lesson_title: One Brick, Eight Bricks: The Scale Factor k
hook_text: Double every side of a box and the volume doesn't double. It multiplies by EIGHT.
clip_script: Now make the brick twice as big in every direction. Here is the picture that locks the rule in forever: to build that double-size brick out of original bricks, you need two along the length, two across the width, and two up the height. Two times two times two — eight original bricks. Not two, not four: eight. Double everything, and volume multiplies by eight, which is two cubed. If you tripled everything, you would need three by three by three — twenty-seven bricks.
visual_style: A single glowing brick multiplying into a 2 by 2 by 2 stack, then exploding into a 3 by 3 by 3 cube of twenty-seven, with counters ticking 2, 4, 8, then 27.
pacing: Deliberate build through the three doublings, rapid-fire payoff on the tripling.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never fall for the doubling trap again.
